body.x: Measuring continence events after they occur does little to predict the next one or to adapt support to the person.
Wearable sensors, real-world data collected over time and AI are meant to move continence care from recording events toward prediction and personalization.

LifeSense Group B.V., a Dutch digital health company led by CEO Valer Pop, builds its work around that shift. Founded in 2015 as a spin-off from Holst Centre, the open-innovation initiative of imec and TNO, the company develops non-invasive wearable technologies and digital solutions for continence care across different stages of life. In 2026, its LifeSense AI Continence Platform was selected as a winner of the KES 2026 Innovation Awards in the Digital Health & Lifestyle category.

The platform connects non-invasive wearable sensing with mobile applications, real-world data and AI. It brings together LifeSense's three product lines: Oopsie Heroes for children, Carin for women and Wil Wear for men. The platform combines wearable sensing, longitudinal real-world data, AI-driven insights and personalized digital support.
At KES 2026, LifeSense is presenting the platform together with Oopsie Heroes, Carin and Wil Wear.

According to the company, LifeSense solutions have reached users in more than 80 countries across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and other markets. Oopsie Heroes alone has produced a real-world dataset from more than 18,900 children and over 1 million data points, which the company uses as a foundation for increasingly personalized and predictive digital support. LifeSense works with international healthcare, research and distribution partners and has expanded into markets including Australia, Japan, South Korea and Singapore.

LifeSense's next phase is to scale from individual connected products to an integrated continence intelligence platform. The company plans to develop its AI-driven prediction and personalization further, add professional connected-care capabilities and grow its international partner network, with Asia as a key region. It already has activities and partnerships in South Korea, Japan, China, Australia, Singapore and Indonesia.

At KES, LifeSense aims to strengthen its presence in South Korea and the wider Asian market. It says South Korea stands out for its advanced digital-health and consumer-electronics ecosystem and its openness to connected healthcare technologies. The company is looking for healthcare, distribution, technology and strategic partners that can combine market access with healthcare knowledge, regulatory expertise and support for professional adoption.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Its Digital Health & Lifestyle sector covers AI-powered healthcare, smart medical devices, digital therapeutics (DTx), health data and platforms, senior and wellness technologies, and accessibility and monitoring solutions. The KES Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13, and KES Match business meetings with domestic buyers, global buyers and investors run from Oct. 14 to Oct. 16.
